Long story short, I'm getting older and I stayed up for well over 24 hours before going into work the next day. As a Customer Service rep, all of my work is done through a ticket system like JIRA or ZenDesk. I kept nodding off as I was responding to tickets (or at least trying to), and I would suddenly jolt awake when my chin hit my chest or I started to feel like I was falling. I would jolt awake to stare at my screen and discovered that I typed what I thought was jibberish into the tickets (luckily I never sent one!). I deleted all except for the one that clued me in to what was going on, which I emailed to myself. You can read it below--names have been changed.

"It's dark. We're waiting for the others. Who? (Guy I know, other guy I know) and the rest of them. Look back behind me, over my shoulder. Oh hey, it's (woman I know). That's funny, I thought she was in Sweden. She's telling me not to worry, they're just a little late. It got dark really fast though. How did (woman I know) get here? The last thing I remember is being at work--why can't I remember when I left? (Woman I know) is lighting a cigarette, but she doesn't smoke anymore. I smile as I remember just how much I really miss (woman I know). Something's not right. First there was work and I remember being really tired and then I was here. Something's wrong. Something's not right. I can't remember. Kind of reminds me of when I dream. Forgot to call (second woman I know). My cellphone's in my pocket, I should call (second woman I know). I reach into my pocket and pull out my phone, but I can't read the numbers. I mean, I know what the numbers are, but I can't actually see them. Fuck I'm dreaming. I should wake up. Wake up. Wake up. Okay."

The thing that freaks me out is not only how much I typed out, but how few typos there actually were. Usually, I'll make a few that I need to go back and correct. The grammar is shit, but the rest?
